data.body: Research R16b7d15f12. Problem: CHANGELOG/RESEARCH/README and regenerated files are touched by every item, so leases collide (claims refused) or agents commit them unleased and the hook warning becomes noise; real conflicts then surface only at merge. Options: (A, recommended) [lease].shared_globs = [...] (default empty): a path matching it is exempt from glob_clash between leases (claim, update, wait, plan), and the commit hook counts it covered for any live lease holder; 'ddflow adopt'/doctor offers a 'merge=union' .gitattributes line for each shared glob that is append-only (git probe: two CHANGELOG prepends merge cleanly), and doctor WARNS for a shared glob with no merge driver (a generated file must be regenerated at merge, not unioned -- union interleaves). (B) a per-item 'append' glob prefix (e.g. '+docs/CHANGELOG.md') meaning shared for this claim only -- more flexible, but every agent must remember it and one forgetting it still collides. (C) status quo + docs: keep these files out of item globs and have the merge step (or one owner item) write them -- no code, but CHANGELOG entries are lost or serialised. Second half of the bug, independent of the choice: the pre-commit lease check should ignore paths whose staged content equals the base branch's (a merge-from-main commit listed main's already-merged paths as unleased) -- that one is a plain bug fix in services/enforce.py and can be split out. Needs: operator picks A/B/C (and whether merge=union is written automatically or only advised).

data.summary: A heartbeat that revives a lapsed lease catches up its globs but not its resources: update --resources made while the lease had lapsed reaches item.resources only (plan_retarget leaves an expired lease alone), and api/lifecycle._catch_up_globs re-syncs globs only, so a raised reservation stays under-counted by resource_shortfall. Fixing it needs claim --resources to write item.resources too (else the catch-up would undo a claim-time override, as Bbd07ab69fd does for globs). data.body: Decision D-shared-globs (operator, option A, merge=union written automatically). Research R16b7d15f12. (1) config: [lease].shared_globs -- paths many items may edit whose merge ddflow does NOT decide (generated files: regenerate after merging); [lease].append_only_globs -- shared too, and ddflow writes '<glob> merge=union' to .gitattributes for each (CHANGELOG-style files; git probe: two prepends merge cleanly). A generated file never gets merge=union (union interleaves). (2) core/schedule: conflicts() skips a glob inside a shared or append-only glob, on both sides; used by plan's blocker and leases.glob_clash (claim, update, wait). (3) enforce.check_commit: a staged path inside a shared glob counts as covered for any agent holding a live lease. (4) services/shared_files.sync_attributes: idempotent append of the missing union lines (adopt._append_once), returning what it added; called by api.setup.configure after a successful --set/--append-toml (CLI config and MCP ddflow_configure: the moment the setting changes, in the same tree as config.toml, so both land in one commit) and by adopt.init_files (init/adopt, which re-syncs a hand-edited config); each prints the lines it added. (5) doctor: a PROBLEM for an append-only glob whose union line is missing (remedy names the command), a NOTE for a shared glob with no merge attribute in .gitattributes. The commit-hook 'paths a merge from main brought in' warning is a separate task (B-fix-hook-merge-from-base).

D-shared-globs records the operator's choice. tests/test_shared_globs.py against the unfixed tree (stub shared_files): 9 failed -- the knobs did not exist, overlapping claims on a changelog were refused, the hook reported it uncovered, nothing wrote .gitattributes

D-shared-globs (accepted, operator) followed: option A, merge=union written by ddflow, doctor warns for a generated shared file, hook merge-from-main split to B-fix-hook-merge-from-base; D-no-own-services-local-dir untouched (.gitattributes is project policy, committed)

titles: ddflow/api/setup.py — `configure` calls `_sync_attributes(repo)` unconditionally after a `--local` edit
ddflow/services/leases.py:183 (glob_clash, the `pairs = conflicts(globs, lease.globs, schedule.shared_globs(cfg))` line)

evidence.note: 2470bed..1e1560c: [lease] shared_globs/append_only_globs (config, documented); core/schedule.conflicts skips globs inside a shared glob, matched as gitattributes matches (gitignore rules, verified against git check-attr); plan blocker + leases.glob_clash use it; enforce.check_commit counts a shared path covered for any live holder; services/shared_files: sync_attributes writes '<glob> merge=union' for COMMITTED append-only globs git gives no driver (asked of git check-attr over every covered tracked file), called by api.setup.configure on --set/--append-toml (not --local) and by adopt.init_files (init/adopt), each printing what it added; findings -> doctor (missing union = PROBLEM, shared generated glob with no driver = NOTE, non-union driver on append-only = NOTE, unreadable glob / glob with whitespace = PROBLEM); README section + knob count. 26 tests.

Final commit not re-run through roborev: a doctor message + test.
full suite at 1e1560c: 3213 passed, 1 skipped, 1 xfailed

Probed against git check-attr: ** boundaries, [!..]/[^..], ]-first classes, depth-free patterns, later broader patterns overriding; local vs committed config; idempotent re-set; hand-edited config re-synced by init; project-chosen driver kept; spaced glob; uncompilable glob. Known trade-off: an append-only glob's union line appended after a narrower project driver (docs/README.md merge=ours under docs/*.md) overrides it for that file -- the operator declared the whole glob append-only.

One shared predicate (schedule.is_shared/shared_globs) for plan, glob_clash and the hook; .gitattributes appends reuse adopt._append_once; config edits route through the single api.setup.configure (CLI + MCP)
